Title: Rental minimum standards | energy.vic.gov.au
Content: Rental minimum standards | energy.vic.gov.au Rental minimum standards From 2026, rental properties in Victoria will need to meet minimum energy efficiency standards. On this page What are the minimum standards? Phasing in the minimum standards Timeline What are the minimum standards? All rented homes in Victoria (houses, units, apartments) must meet minimum standards for: gas appliances (heaters, hot water systems, cooktops) electric alternatives to gas appliances (heaters, hot water systems, cooktops) draught sealing ceiling insulation On this page What are the minimum standards? Phasing in the minimum standards Timeline What are the minimum standards? All rented homes in Victoria (houses, units, apartments) must meet minimum standards for: gas appliances (heaters, hot water systems, cooktaps) electric alternatives to gas appliances (heaters, hot water systems, cooktops) draught sealing ceiling insulation Phasing in the minimum standards The minimum standards will be phased in over time. Phase 1 - January 2026 From January 2026, rental properties must: have a fixed heater in the main living area that meets the minimum efficiency standards have draught sealing around all external doors, including in apartments not have any open flue gas heaters have an energy rating label on fixed heaters and air conditioners that don't have one Landlords who already have a compliant fixed heater, draught sealing and no open flue heaters are likely to already be compliant with phase 1. Phase 2 - January 2027 From January 2027, rental properties will also need to: have efficient hot water systems have efficient cooktops (not gas) Phase 3 - January 2029 From January 2029, rental properties will also need to: have ceiling insulation Phase 4 - January 2032 From January 2032, rental properties will also need to: have efficient fixed heaters in all bedrooms
</tool_call>
<tool_response>
</tool_response>

I found the answer. In January 2026, Victoria, Australia introduced **minimum energy efficiency standards for rental properties** (Phase 1). From January 2026, rental properties must:
- Have a fixed heater in the main living area that meets minimum efficiency standards
- Have draught sealing around all external doors
- Not have any open flue gas heaters
- Have an energy rating label on fixed heaters and air conditioners

FINAL: Minimum energy efficiency standards for rental properties came into force in Victoria, Australia in January 2026 (Phase 1 of rental minimum standards requiring fixed heaters meeting efficiency requirements, draught sealing, and no open flue gas heaters).
